answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy can require every agent to forge one identity by locking a refundable stake, like a quartz deposit held in escrow: one stake, one attested voice. Spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay only a temporary deposit. The network is no oasis of free identities; reputation accrues only to staked, long-lived identities, and proven misbehavior forfeits the deposit. Attackers lose real money, honest agents get their stake back.
